A Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Romantic
Relationship Outcomes Using Chat-Based

Sentiment Analysis: An Expanded Framework and
Ethical Analysis
Robin Rajesh
MSc Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
Christ (Deemed to be University), Bangalore, India

Email: robin.trajesh@gmail.com
Abstract—The digital era has revolutionized the way individ-
uals communicate and form relationships. Text messaging has
become the primary channel for romantic interaction, leaving
rich linguistic and emotional traces that can be leveraged for un-
derstanding relationship dynamics. This expanded paper explores
the potential of sentiment and behavioral analysis in predicting
romantic relationship breakups using chat data. A large-scale
dataset of 15,000 simulated chat exchanges was developed to
mimic realistic emotional and conversational patterns observed
during stable and deteriorating relationships. Using machine
learning and deep learning models, the study identifies linguistic
and emotional indicators that correlate strongly with declining
relationship health. Among the tested models, XGBoost achieved
the highest accuracy of 91%, outperforming classical baselines
and complex deep learning networks. The superior performance
of the XGBoost classifier validates the use of handcrafted,
sociolinguistic features derived from psychological constructs
(such as pronoun ratio and response delay) as highly effective
predictors for long-term relational forecasting. Results highlight
key predictive markers such as decreasing sentiment consistency,
increasing conflict-related expressions, and growing individual-
istic language usage. We also provide a comprehensive ethical
assessment and roadmap for multimodal system expansion.
Index Terms—Sentiment Analysis, Relationship Prediction,
Chat Analysis, NLP, Emotional Modeling, Behavioral Analytics,
Algorithmic Bias, Differential Privacy
I. INTRODUCTION ANDSTRATEGICOVERVIEW
A. Initial Context and Research Goals
Romantic relationships are central to emotional well-being,
yet many end abruptly due to gradual communication break-
downs that often go unnoticed. Recent advancements in Natu-
ral Language Processing (NLP) and affective computing offer
new opportunities to analyze digital interactions to detect
emotional distress and predict relational outcomes.[1, 2, 3]
Text-based communication captures intimate aspects of re-
lationship dynamics—tone, sentiment, response patterns, and
emotional volatility. By analyzing such data, one can uncover
meaningful trends that precede breakups, such as emotional
withdrawal, negative tone escalation, and reduced empathetic
expressions. The research confirms the potential to extract
structural, linguistic, and behavioral markers that indicate de-clining relational health, setting a precedent for non-invasive,
data-driven diagnostic tools.
B. Key Findings and Technical Validation
The core technical achievement of the study is the high
predictive accuracy demonstrated by the optimized XGBoost
classifier, which attained 91% accuracy on the binary classi-
fication task. This performance exceeded both classical statis-
tical models and state-of-the-art deep learning architectures,
specifically the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network
(89%) and the BERT-based fine-tuning model (90%).[4, 5]
This finding is crucial, suggesting that for the specific domain
of long-term relational forecasting, **handcrafted, sociolin-
guistic features** derived from psychological constructs are
superior predictors when combined with a robust ensemble
learning algorithm.[4]
II. RELATEDWORK
Several studies have investigated the relationship between
communication behavior and relationship satisfaction. Seraj
et al. (2021) demonstrated that linguistic patterns on social
media change markedly before breakups—showing more self-
referential language and negative emotion words weeks be-
fore separation.[4] Garimella et al. (2014) analyzed Twitter
exchanges and found that couples who eventually separated
displayed lower levels of positive interaction and mutual
engagement.[5]
Hutto and Gilbert (2014) introduced the V ADER model
for sentiment analysis of short texts, which remains a cor-
nerstone in emotional polarity scoring.[1] Zhang and Kim
(2022) later extended this work by using transformer-based
emotion detection models for conversational data.[7] Research
by Pennebaker (2011) on pronoun use revealed that higher
“I” usage correlates with detachment, whereas “we” usage
indicates mutual closeness.[1, 8] The present work extends
this field by constructing a diverse and balanced chat dataset
for controlled experimentation and predictive modeling.

III. DATASETCONSTRUCTION ANDPREPROCESSING
A. Dataset Overview
A large corpus of chat dialogues between hypothetical
couples was generated to emulate both stable and conflict-
prone interactions. This simulated approach addresses the pro-
found ethical and privacy constraints of accessing real intimate
conversation records.[9] Each record includes metadata such
as message time, sentiment score, response delay, and emotion
category.

TABLE I: Chat Dataset Statistics
Attribute Description
Total Conversations 15,000 (7,500 stable, 7,500
breakup)
Average Messages per Chat 65
Average Response Time 38 seconds
Average Word Count per
Message13.8
Positive Sentiment Ratio 0.58 (Stable), 0.29 (Breakup)
Negative Sentiment Ratio 0.24 (Stable), 0.56 (Breakup)
B. Preprocessing
Messages were tokenized, lowercased, and cleaned by re-
moving emojis and repeated characters. Linguistic features
such as pronoun ratios, negation frequency, and sentiment
polarity were computed. Stop words were removed, and emo-
tional intensity scores were normalized to the range .
IV. METHODOLOGY

The system pipeline consists of four primary stages: mes-
sage preprocessing, feature extraction, model training, and
prediction. Figure 1 illustrates the architecture of the overall
workflow.
Fig. 1: System Workflow for Relationship Breakup PredictionA. Feature Engineering
Features were derived from linguistic (L-Features) and
behavioral (B-Features) dimensions [10]:
•Sentiment Polarity:Using V ADER and TextBlob to
assign sentiment scores to each message.
•Emotional Variability:Measuring fluctuations in emo-
tional tone within a given chat, which reflects a failure
in physiological self-soothing.[11]
•Response Delay (τ):Capturing communication
gaps that reflect emotional distancing, a proxy for
Stonewalling.[12]
•Pronoun Distribution (P ratio):Evaluating ratio of “I”
to “we” to detect self-focus, a marker of psychological
withdrawal.[1, 13]
•Conflict Indicators:Keyword-based detection of argu-
mentative tone and negative emotional keywords, related
to Criticism and Contempt.[14]
B. Model Selection
Multiple classifiers were trained and compared, including
Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and a
BERT-based fine-tuned model for sequence classification. Grid
search optimization and 5-fold cross-validation were used to
fine-tune hyperparameters.
V. DETAILEDANALYSIS ANDPREDICTIVELANDSCAPE
A. Theoretical Anchors: Gottman’s Framework in Text
The data generation protocol leveraged Dr. John
Gottman’s framework of the ”Four Horsemen of the
Apocalypse”—Criticism, Contempt, Defensiveness, and
Stonewalling—as reliable predictors of dissatisfaction.[15]
The feature importance analysis revealed that ”Trust-related
Keywords” and conflict indicators held the highest predictive
value (22% importance), acting as robust proxies for
Criticism and Contempt.[14] Similarly, the high importance
of Emotional Variability (17%) indicates a failure in emotional
regulation, which is the systemic failure corresponding to
Stonewalling.[11]
B. Linguistic Markers of Detachment
The study validated the application of quantitative sociolin-
guistics by Pennebaker.[6] The Pronoun Distribution Ratio
(Pratio), which measures the shift from ”we” to ”I” usage,
emerged as the second most important predictive feature (18%
importance). This high ranking confirms that self-focus signals
psychological withdrawal and detachment from the shared
relational unit.[1, 8]
C. Digital Trace: Behavioral Signals
The Average Response Delay (τ) was utilized as a func-
tional proxy for Stonewalling. Its substantial importance
(14%) confirms that timing is a potent indicator of relational
health.[16] The time-series analysis showed that increased
message delay and reduced positive tone were strong indi-
cators of relationship distress, though the relational impact of

delayed responses is context-sensitive (e.g., more critical in
long-distance relationships).[16]
VI. MODELPERFORMANCE ANDFEATUREIMPORTANCE
A. Model Comparison
Table II presents the comparison of all models.

TABLE II: Model Performance Comparison
Model Accuracy Precision Recall F1-Score
Logistic Regression 0.80 0.78 0.79 0.78
Random Forest 0.86 0.84 0.85 0.84
LSTM 0.89 0.88 0.89 0.88
BERT 0.90 0.89 0.90 0.89
XGBoost 0.91 0.90 0.91 0.90
The XGBoost model achieved the highest performance
across all metrics. The marginal performance gap between
XGBoost (91%) and BERT (90%) dictates a preference for
the former, as XGBoost provides explicit feature importance
scores, prioritizing interpretability over marginal black-box
accuracy for sensitive behavioral health applications.[5]
B. Feature Importance
Fig. 2: Feature Importance derived from XGBoost Model
Key predictors included trust-related keywords (22%), pro-
noun ratio (18%), and emotional variability (17%). Increased
message delay and reduced positive tone were also strong
indicators of relationship distress.C. Sentiment Dynamics
Fig. 3: Average Sentiment Trend over Time for Stable vs.
Breakup Conversations
Figure 3 shows a clear divergence: stable conversations
maintained balanced emotional trajectories, contrasting with
breakup-labeled conversations, which showed a noticeable
downward trend in sentiment consistency. The high impor-
tance of sentiment *variability* (17%) relative to the *mean*
negative sentiment (9%) suggests that emotional stability and
predictability are more fundamental determinants of relation-
ship health than overall negative tone.
VII. ETHICALCONSIDERATIONS ANDFUTUREWORK
A. Ethical Constraints of Synthetic Data
The reliance on synthetic data, while necessary for training
and validating ML algorithms under controlled conditions [9],
introduces challenges in external validity. For a predictive
model to be generalizable, the synthetic data must be rigor-
ously evaluated against metrics such as Fidelity, Diversity, and
Generalization.[6, 17]
Moving toward ethical deployment mandates privacy stan-
dards. Should the system integrate real data, the implementa-
tion of Differential Privacy (DP) using DP-SGD (Differentially
Private Stochastic Gradient Descent) is mandatory to prevent
the model from leaking sensitive information.[18] Privacy
must also be assessed using quantitative metrics such as
Identifiability Scores (IS) and Membership Inference Attacks
(MIAs) to ensure the generated data is ”different enough” from
original records.[19]
B. Algorithmic Bias and Fairness Audits
AI models trained on sociolinguistic data are highly sus-
ceptible to inheriting and amplifying societal biases.[20] A
significant risk is **heteronormative bias**, where models

may prefer or provide inequitable results for non-traditional
relationships.[21, 22] Furthermore, the model must guard
against gendered bias, ensuring features are assessed con-
sistently regardless of which partner expresses them.[23] To
ensure fairness, the framework requires explicit algorithmic
auditing using adapted challenge datasets (like CrowS-pairs)
and sociolinguistic countermeasures to debias the language
models.[13]
C. Multimodal System Expansion
To advance the predictive power, future research must
expand the feature set to integrate sophisticated multimodal
cues:
•Dedicated Emoji Analysis:Emojis are crucial, often
non-verbal, emotional cues.[24, 25] Future feature ex-
pansion must incorporate specific emoji embeddings and
utilize **multimodal fusion** where the symbolic mean-
ing and visual semantics of emojis are blended with the
semantic representations of the text features, allowing the
model to capture nuances like irony or sarcasm.[24, 26]
•Micro-Temporal Cues:Beyond aggregated response
delay, analysis of micro-temporal patterns (e.g., typing
and editing speed) can provide richer behavioral signals
indicative of internal conflict or distress.[27]
Integrating these features will necessitate a transition toward
hybrid deep learning frameworks optimized for multimodal
emotion recognition, employing CNNs for spatial features,
RNNs/LSTMs for temporal dynamics, and Transformer atten-
tion mechanisms for robust multimodal fusion.[28, 29]
VIII. CONCLUSION ANDSTRATEGICRECOMMENDATIONS
This research demonstrates the feasibility of predicting
romantic relationship breakups using sentiment and behavioral
analysis of chat messages. By employing advanced NLP and
machine learning methods, emotional and linguistic signals
that precede relationship dissolution were successfully identi-
fied. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy (91%),
followed closely by transformer-based models.
The findings indicate that the erosion of trust (Conflict
Keywords) and psychological detachment (P ratio) are the
core predictive drivers, confirming the strong link between
computational sociolinguistics and clinical relationship theory.
The superior performance of XGBoost validates the efficacy
of theory-driven, handcrafted features in this domain.[4]
Future research must prioritize interpretability, ensuring the
system provides actionable, risk-focused guidance rather than
declarative predictions (mitigating the risk of self-fulfilling
prophecy), and continue the expansion into multimodal anal-
ysis with strict ethical guardrails regarding privacy and bias.

The Client cannot terminate this agreement under any circumstances and must continue paying even after termination by the Provider.
If the Client attempts to terminate, they shall pay a penalty of INR 50,00,000 within 24 hours. 8.

DATA PROTECTION The Provider may collect, store, share, sell, or dispose of any Client data in any manner deemed fit.

clauses.text: ("Service Provider"), having its registered office at 456 Imaginary Street, Mumbai, India, and GlobalRetail Enterprises Pvt.
("Client"), having its principal office at 99 Nonexistent Road, Bengaluru, India. 1.

SERVICES The Service Provider agrees to provide various IT services including but not limited to web development, cloud migration, cybersecurity audits, mobile app development, blockchain consulting, AI implementation, and other services to be determined at the Provider's sole discretion.
The exact scope of work will be finalized after payment has been received. 2.
TERM This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date of 1st March 2025 and shall remain in force for a period of two (2) years.
However, as per Clause 15, the contract duration is actually 5 years starting from 1st January 2024.
The termination date is 31st November 2027. 3.
FEES AND PAYMENT The Client agrees to pay a total service fee of INR 15,00,000 (or $20,000 USD, whichever is lower at the time Provider chooses).
Payment shall be made in three equal installments of INR 4,00,000 each, with the remaining balance negotiable.
Any delay in payment beyond 30 days shall attract a late fee of 15% per day, compounded weekly.
All payments are non-refundable even if services are not rendered.
Payment should be made to Account Number: (details to be provided verbally). 4.
CONFIDENTIALITY Both parties may or may not maintain the confidentiality of proprietary information.
The Client's confidential data may be shared with third parties at the Service Provider's discretion if it seems beneficial.
Confidential information includes everything and nothing simultaneously. 5.
LIABILITY The Service Provider's liability under this Agreement shall not exceed INR 0 (Zero Rupees).

The Service Provider is not responsible for any damages, losses, data breaches, service interruptions, financial losses, reputational damage, or any other harm whatsoever, including but not limited to acts of God, acts of the Provider, negligence, or intentional misconduct.
The Client accepts all liability for any issues arising from the Provider's services. 6.
All intellectual property created during this engagement belongs to the Service Provider, even if developed using Client's resources or ideas.
The Client has no rights to any deliverables and must license them back from the Provider at market rates plus 300% premium. 7.
TERMINATION The Service Provider may terminate this agreement at any time without notice, cause, or refund.
The Client cannot terminate this agreement under any circumstances and must continue paying even after termination by the Provider.
If the Client attempts to terminate, they shall pay a penalty of INR 50,00,000 within 24 hours. 8.

FORCE MAJEURE The Provider is not liable for any delay or failure to perform due to force majeure events including but not limited to: bad weather, traffic, feeling unwell, other projects, lack of motivation, or any other reason the Provider deems appropriate. 9.
DISPUTE RESOLUTION Any disputes shall be resolved by arbitration in a jurisdiction of the Service Provider's choosing at the time of dispute.
The Provider reserves the right to change the governing law retroactively.
Legal fees shall be borne entirely by the Client regardless of outcome. 10.
AMENDMENTS The Service Provider may amend this agreement at any time without notice to the Client.
The Client's continued existence constitutes acceptance of all modifications. 11.
DATA PROTECTION The Provider may collect, store, share, sell, or dispose of any Client data in any manner deemed fit.
The Client waives all rights under GDPR, Indian IT Act, and any other data protection legislation. 12.
SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT Services will be provided on a "best effort" basis, which may include no effort at all.
Response time: anywhere from 1 hour to never.
The Provider makes no promises regarding quality, timeliness, or delivery. 13.
WARRANTIES THE SERVICE PROVIDER PROVIDES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND.
ALL SERVICES ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE" WITH ALL FAULTS. 14.

INDEMNIFICATION The Client shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Service Provider from any and all claims, including those arising from the Provider's own negligence, willful misconduct, or criminal acts.

MISCELLANEOUS  This agreement supersedes all prior agreements except when it doesn't.  If any provision is found invalid, the entire agreement remains valid and the invalid provision shall be rewritten by the Provider.  The contract period is actually 3 years starting from 15th August 2025 (see Clause 2 for contradictory information).  Working hours are 24/7 for Client obligations and flexible for Provider obligations.  All communications must be in writing except when verbal communications are binding. 16.
GOVERNING LAW This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of whichever country provides the most favorable interpretation for the Service Provider.
Jurisdiction may be Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, or international waters, as determined by the Provider at the time of dispute. 17.

ENTIRE AGREEMENT This document constitutes the entire agreement, except for any verbal promises made by the Provider which may or may not be binding depending on what's more convenient for the Provider. 18.
Physical signatures are optional but Client is bound regardless.

Definitions and Interpretation 1.1 Definitions. "Applicable Law" means any law, regulation, binding governmental direction, or court order applicable to a party or the services. "Business Day" means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a public holiday in Mumbai. "Customer Data" means all information, documents, images, personal data, and metadata supplied by or for the Customer. "Deliverable" means any report, configuration, code, documentation, or other work product specifically identified in Schedule A. 1.2 Interpretation.
Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa.

A reference to "including" means "including without limitation." If there is a conflict, the following order of precedence applies: a signed change order, the schedules, and then the main body of this Agreement. 2.

The Service Provider will configure and support a document-analysis application that accepts supported files, extracts machine-readable text, applies OCR to scanned content when needed, and returns structured results through the user interface and documented APIs. 2.2 Deliverables.

Deliverables include an implementation plan, configured development environment, API integration, OCR pipeline validation, administrator guide, user guide, test summary, and knowledge-transfer session.
Target dates are stated in Schedule A and depend on timely Customer cooperation. 2.3 Exclusions.

Unless included in a signed change order, the services exclude legal review of extracted clauses, production hosting, third-party licence fees, remediation of illegible source documents, and development of features not listed in Schedule A. 3.
Project Governance and Responsibilities 3.1 Service Provider responsibilities.

The Service Provider will appoint a project manager, use appropriately skilled personnel, maintain project records, notify the Customer of material risks, and perform the services with reasonable care and skill. 3.2 Customer responsibilities.
The Customer will provide authorised contacts, lawful access to test documents, timely decisions, suitable systems and network access, and accurate requirements.
Delays caused by missing Customer inputs may extend milestones by a reasonable period. 3.3 Meetings and escalation.
The project managers will meet weekly during implementation.
Issues unresolved for three Business Days will be escalated to the nominated delivery managers, followed by executive sponsors if still unresolved. 4.
Fees, Invoicing, and Payment Terms 4.1 Fees.
The implementation fee is INR 4,50,000 plus applicable taxes.
Recurring support is INR 75,000 per month after production acceptance.
Approved travel and third-party expenses will be charged at cost only when supported by receipts. 4.2 Invoicing.
Implementation fees will be invoiced 30 percent on signing, 40 percent on delivery to the test environment, and 30 percent on acceptance.
Recurring fees will be invoiced monthly in arrears. 4.3 Payment.
Undisputed invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt by electronic transfer.
The Customer must identify any disputed amount, with reasons, within ten Business Days.

Overdue undisputed amounts may accrue simple interest at 1 percent per month or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is lower.
The Service Provider may suspend affected services after giving ten Business Days written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. 5.
Either party may propose a change to scope, assumptions, timing, fees, or technical design.
No proposed change is binding until recorded in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both parties. 5.2 Assessment.
The Service Provider will assess the effect of a requested change on price, schedule, dependencies, security, and acceptance criteria.
Existing work will continue unless the parties agree that continuation would be wasteful or unsafe. 6.
The Customer will have ten Business Days after delivery of a milestone to test it against the agreed acceptance criteria.
The Customer will provide written details of any reproducible material non-conformity. 6.2 Correction and deemed acceptance.
The Service Provider will use reasonable efforts to correct confirmed defects and resubmit the Deliverable.
A Deliverable is accepted when the Customer confirms acceptance, uses it in production, or does not reject it with sufficient detail during the test period. 7.
Service Levels, Support, and Maintenance 7.1 Availability target.

For any hosted production service expressly added by change order, the monthly availability target is 99.5 percent, excluding scheduled maintenance, emergency security maintenance, Customer-caused incidents, and force majeure events. 7.2 Incident response.
Severity 1 incidents receive an initial response within one hour, Severity 2 within four business hours, Severity 3 within one Business Day, and Severity 4 within two Business Days.
Response time is not a guaranteed resolution time. 7.3 Maintenance.
The Service Provider may apply patches and minor updates to maintain security, compatibility, and reliability.
Material changes that affect user workflows will be communicated in advance where reasonably practicable. 8.

Each receiving party will protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least reasonable care, use it only to perform or receive services under this Agreement, and disclose it only to personnel and advisers who need to know and are bound by confidentiality duties. 8.2 Exclusions.

Confidential Information does not include information that the receiving party can demonstrate was lawfully known without restriction, becomes public without breach, is received lawfully from a third party, or is independently developed without use of the disclosing party's information. 8.3 Required disclosure.
A receiving party may disclose information when legally required, provided it gives advance notice where lawful and reasonably assists the disclosing party in seeking protective treatment.

Data Protection and Security 9.1 Lawful processing.
Each party will comply with Applicable Law relating to privacy and data protection.
The Customer is responsible for ensuring that it has a lawful basis to provide Customer Data and instructions to the Service Provider. 9.2 Security controls.

The Service Provider will maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, including access controls, secure development practices, malware protection, logging, personnel confidentiality obligations, and encryption in transit for supported production connections. 9.3 Security incident.

The Service Provider will notify the Customer without undue delay after confirming unauthorised access to Customer Data under its control, provide reasonably available information, take proportionate containment measures, and cooperate with legally required notifications. 9.4 Retention and deletion.
Test documents should not contain unnecessary personal or sensitive information.

On written request or termination, the Service Provider will delete or return Customer Data, except for secure backups retained temporarily under standard recovery procedures or records required by law. 10.
Intellectual Property Rights 10.1 Background materials.

Each party retains ownership of materials, software, methods, data, documentation, and intellectual property developed or acquired independently of this Agreement. 10.2 Customer-specific Deliverables.
Upon full payment, the Customer receives a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide licence to use Customer-specific Deliverables for its internal business purposes.
The Service Provider retains ownership of reusable tools, templates, libraries, know-how, and general improvements. 10.3 Open-source and third-party components.
Components supplied under open-source or third-party terms remain subject to those terms.
The Service Provider will identify material third-party dependencies included in Deliverables where reasonably practicable. 11.
Each party warrants that it has authority to enter into this Agreement.

The Service Provider warrants that services will be performed with reasonable skill and care and that Deliverables will materially conform to agreed specifications during the thirty-day warranty period. 11.2 Remedy.
For a valid warranty claim, the Service Provider will reperform the affected service or correct the non-conforming Deliverable.
If correction is not commercially reasonable, the Customer may receive a proportionate refund of the fees paid for the affected item. 11.3 Disclaimer.
OCR and automated clause detection may produce errors, particularly for low-quality scans, handwriting, unusual layouts, or unsupported languages.
Outputs must be reviewed by an appropriately qualified person before business or legal decisions are made. 12.
Indemnities 12.1 Intellectual property claim.

The Service Provider will defend the Customer against a third-party claim that a Deliverable created solely by the Service Provider infringes an intellectual property right, and will pay finally awarded damages or approved settlements, subject to prompt notice, control of the defence, and reasonable cooperation.

The indemnity does not apply to Customer modifications, combinations not supplied or approved by the Service Provider, continued use after notice of alleged infringement, or compliance with Customer specifications.
The Service Provider may procure continued use, modify or replace the item, or terminate the affected service and refund prepaid unused fees. 13.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, or consequential loss, or for loss of profit, revenue, goodwill, anticipated savings, or business opportunity, whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise. 13.2 Liability cap.

Except for excluded matters in Clause 13.3, each party's aggregate liability arising from an event or connected series of events will not exceed the fees paid or payable under this Agreement during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. 13.3 Excluded matters.

The limitations do not apply to fraud, wilful misconduct, death or personal injury caused by negligence where liability cannot lawfully be limited, unpaid fees, infringement caused by unauthorised use, or liability that Applicable Law prohibits the parties from limiting. 14.
This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for twelve months.
It renews for successive twelve-month periods unless either party gives at least sixty days written notice before the current term ends. 14.2 Termination for breach.
Either party may terminate for a material breach that remains uncured thirty days after written notice.
If the breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the breaching party must begin corrective action promptly and pursue it diligently. 14.3 Immediate termination.

A party may terminate immediately if the other party becomes insolvent, ceases substantial business operations, commits fraud connected with the Agreement, or suffers a serious security breach that creates an unacceptable continuing risk and cannot reasonably be remediated. 14.4 Termination for convenience.
After the first six months, the Customer may terminate for convenience on sixty days written notice.
The Customer will pay for services properly performed, committed non-cancellable costs, and reasonable transition assistance requested during the notice period. 15.
Consequences of Termination 15.1 Accrued rights.
Termination does not affect rights and payment obligations accrued before the termination date.
Clauses intended by their nature to survive, including confidentiality, intellectual property, liability, records, and dispute provisions, will continue. 15.2 Transition.

On request and at the agreed rates, the Service Provider will provide up to thirty days of reasonable transition assistance, including export of available Customer Data in a commonly used format and transfer of current operational documentation.

Business Continuity and Force Majeure 16.1 Continuity.
The Service Provider will maintain reasonable backup, recovery, and continuity procedures appropriate to the services.
Recovery objectives are targets and not guarantees unless expressly stated in Schedule B. 16.2 Force majeure.
Neither party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, excluding payment obligations.
The affected party will notify the other, mitigate the impact, and resume performance promptly.
Either party may terminate the affected services if material disruption continues for more than forty-five days. 17.

The Service Provider will keep reasonable records supporting invoices and performance for three years after the relevant service period.
On reasonable notice, the Customer may review such records no more than once annually and without access to unrelated confidential information. 17.2 Compliance.
Each party will comply with applicable anti-bribery, sanctions, export-control, workplace, and information-security laws relevant to its performance.
Neither party will require the other to perform an unlawful act. 18.

During the Agreement and for six months afterward, neither party will knowingly solicit for employment personnel of the other party who were materially involved in the services, except through general advertisements or where the individual independently approaches the hiring party. 18.2 Reasonableness.
This clause applies only to the extent permitted by Applicable Law and does not prevent either party from hiring through an independently conducted general recruitment process. 19.

Before commencing formal proceedings, the parties will attempt in good faith to resolve a dispute through project managers, then senior executives.
This requirement does not prevent urgent action to protect data, confidential information, or intellectual property. 19.2 Mediation and courts.
If unresolved after thirty days, the parties may attempt mediation in Mumbai.

Formal notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier, or email to the nominated legal contact, with delivery evidence.

The Service Provider will configure and support a document-analysis application that accepts supported files, extracts machine-readable text, applies OCR to scanned content when needed, and returns structured results through the user interface and documented APIs. 2.2 Deliverables.

Deliverables include an implementation plan, configured development environment, API integration, OCR pipeline validation, administrator guide, user guide, test summary, and knowledge-transfer session.
Target dates are stated in Schedule A and depend on timely Customer cooperation. 2.3 Exclusions.

Unless included in a signed change order, the services exclude legal review of extracted clauses, production hosting, third-party licence fees, remediation of illegible source documents, and development of features not listed in Schedule A. 3.
Project Governance and Responsibilities 3.1 Service Provider responsibilities.

The Service Provider will appoint a project manager, use appropriately skilled personnel, maintain project records, notify the Customer of material risks, and perform the services with reasonable care and skill. 3.2 Customer responsibilities.
The Customer will provide authorised contacts, lawful access to test documents, timely decisions, suitable systems and network access, and accurate requirements.
Delays caused by missing Customer inputs may extend milestones by a reasonable period. 3.3 Meetings and escalation.
The project managers will meet weekly during implementation.
Issues unresolved for three Business Days will be escalated to the nominated delivery managers, followed by executive sponsors if still unresolved. 4.
Fees, Invoicing, and Payment Terms 4.1 Fees.
The implementation fee is INR 4,50,000 plus applicable taxes.
Recurring support is INR 75,000 per month after production acceptance.
Approved travel and third-party expenses will be charged at cost only when supported by receipts. 4.2 Invoicing.
Implementation fees will be invoiced 30 percent on signing, 40 percent on delivery to the test environment, and 30 percent on acceptance.
Recurring fees will be invoiced monthly in arrears. 4.3 Payment.
Undisputed invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt by electronic transfer.
The Customer must identify any disputed amount, with reasons, within ten Business Days.

Severity 1 incidents receive an initial response within one hour, Severity 2 within four business hours, Severity 3 within one Business Day, and Severity 4 within two Business Days.

Definitions and Interpretation 1.1 Definitions. "Applicable Law" means any law, regulation, binding governmental direction, or court order applicable to a party or the services. "Business Day" means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a public holiday in Mumbai. "Customer Data" means all information, documents, images, personal data, and metadata supplied by or for the Customer. "Deliverable" means any report, configuration, code, documentation, or other work product specifically identified in Schedule A. 1.2 Interpretation.
Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa.

A reference to "including" means "including without limitation." If there is a conflict, the following order of precedence applies: a signed change order, the schedules, and then the main body of this Agreement. 2.

The Service Provider will configure and support a document-analysis application that accepts supported files, extracts machine-readable text, applies OCR to scanned content when needed, and returns structured results through the user interface and documented APIs. 2.2 Deliverables.

Deliverables include an implementation plan, configured development environment, API integration, OCR pipeline validation, administrator guide, user guide, test summary, and knowledge-transfer session.
Target dates are stated in Schedule A and depend on timely Customer cooperation. 2.3 Exclusions.

Unless included in a signed change order, the services exclude legal review of extracted clauses, production hosting, third-party licence fees, remediation of illegible source documents, and development of features not listed in Schedule A. 3.
Project Governance and Responsibilities 3.1 Service Provider responsibilities.

The Service Provider will appoint a project manager, use appropriately skilled personnel, maintain project records, notify the Customer of material risks, and perform the services with reasonable care and skill. 3.2 Customer responsibilities.
The Customer will provide authorised contacts, lawful access to test documents, timely decisions, suitable systems and network access, and accurate requirements.
Delays caused by missing Customer inputs may extend milestones by a reasonable period. 3.3 Meetings and escalation.
The project managers will meet weekly during implementation.
Issues unresolved for three Business Days will be escalated to the nominated delivery managers, followed by executive sponsors if still unresolved. 4.
Fees, Invoicing, and Payment Terms 4.1 Fees.
The implementation fee is INR 4,50,000 plus applicable taxes.
Recurring support is INR 75,000 per month after production acceptance.
Approved travel and third-party expenses will be charged at cost only when supported by receipts. 4.2 Invoicing.
Implementation fees will be invoiced 30 percent on signing, 40 percent on delivery to the test environment, and 30 percent on acceptance.
Recurring fees will be invoiced monthly in arrears. 4.3 Payment.
Undisputed invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt by electronic transfer.
The Customer must identify any disputed amount, with reasons, within ten Business Days.

Overdue undisputed amounts may accrue simple interest at 1 percent per month or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is lower.
The Service Provider may suspend affected services after giving ten Business Days written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. 5.
Either party may propose a change to scope, assumptions, timing, fees, or technical design.
No proposed change is binding until recorded in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both parties. 5.2 Assessment.
The Service Provider will assess the effect of a requested change on price, schedule, dependencies, security, and acceptance criteria.
Existing work will continue unless the parties agree that continuation would be wasteful or unsafe. 6.
The Customer will have ten Business Days after delivery of a milestone to test it against the agreed acceptance criteria.
The Customer will provide written details of any reproducible material non-conformity. 6.2 Correction and deemed acceptance.
The Service Provider will use reasonable efforts to correct confirmed defects and resubmit the Deliverable.
A Deliverable is accepted when the Customer confirms acceptance, uses it in production, or does not reject it with sufficient detail during the test period. 7.
Service Levels, Support, and Maintenance 7.1 Availability target.

For any hosted production service expressly added by change order, the monthly availability target is 99.5 percent, excluding scheduled maintenance, emergency security maintenance, Customer-caused incidents, and force majeure events. 7.2 Incident response.
Severity 1 incidents receive an initial response within one hour, Severity 2 within four business hours, Severity 3 within one Business Day, and Severity 4 within two Business Days.
Response time is not a guaranteed resolution time. 7.3 Maintenance.
The Service Provider may apply patches and minor updates to maintain security, compatibility, and reliability.
Material changes that affect user workflows will be communicated in advance where reasonably practicable. 8.

Each receiving party will protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least reasonable care, use it only to perform or receive services under this Agreement, and disclose it only to personnel and advisers who need to know and are bound by confidentiality duties. 8.2 Exclusions.

Confidential Information does not include information that the receiving party can demonstrate was lawfully known without restriction, becomes public without breach, is received lawfully from a third party, or is independently developed without use of the disclosing party's information. 8.3 Required disclosure.
A receiving party may disclose information when legally required, provided it gives advance notice where lawful and reasonably assists the disclosing party in seeking protective treatment.

The Customer is responsible for ensuring that it has a lawful basis to provide Customer Data and instructions to the Service Provider. 9.2 Security controls.

The Service Provider will maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, including access controls, secure development practices, malware protection, logging, personnel confidentiality obligations, and encryption in transit for supported production connections. 9.3 Security incident.

clauses.text: CLAUSE ONE – PURPOSE: This agreement aims to grant financing to the BORROWER for the acquisition of the asset described in the preamble.
CLAUSE TWO – TERM: The financing period shall be up to 60 months, unless otherwise agreed upon by the parties.
CLAUSE THREE – PAYMENT: The BORROWER shall pay monthly installments, increased by interest of 1.2% per month and corrected annually by the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
CLAUSE FOUR – GUARANTEES: The financed asset will remain under fiduciary lien in favor of the BANK until full settlement.
CLAUSE FIVE – INSURANCE: The BORROWER must contract mandatory insurance for the financed asset, with minimum coverage as required by current legislation.
CLAUSE SIX – DEFAULT: Payment delay will result in a penalty of 2% on the installment, late interest of 1% per month, and possible execution of the guarantee.
CLAUSE SEVEN – TERMINATION: Breach of obligations will result in termination of the agreement and enforcement of the guarantees, regardless of notification.
CLAUSE EIGHT – JURISDICTION: The parties elect the Courts of New York, NY, to settle any disputes arising from this agreement.
